faqs.q: What is the Endless Wire Rope Sling and where is it used?
faqs.a: The Endless Wire Rope Sling is an endless steel wire rope sling for lifting with cranes and hoists, listed in sizes 10 mm to 240 mm. Each row gives working loads in kN for single, double-leg and four-leg use at 45 and 90 degrees, with a minimum breaking load of 60 to 29,275 kN.

faqs.q: How do I read Endless Wire Rope Sling part numbers such as IH-LR-WS-END-10MM?
faqs.a: IH-LR-WS-END-10MM is the 10 mm size, 60 kN minimum breaking load, IH-LR-WS-END-114MM the 114 mm size, 6875 kN minimum breaking load and IH-LR-WS-END-240MM the 240 mm size, 29275 kN minimum breaking load. The size table lists every Indus part number with its own dimensions and rating, so quote the full part number rather than the series name.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Endless Wire Rope Sling come in?
faqs.a: The Endless Wire Rope Sling is listed in sizes 10 mm to 240 mm. The size table gives each size its own Indus part number, with rope size, ratings or dimensions for that size.

faqs.q: How should I pick the size of Endless Wire Rope Sling for my job?
faqs.a: Choose on the rated load for the way you will rig it: the angle between legs cuts what each leg may carry, and [our sling angle chart](/blog/sling-angle-chart) shows how. Then pick the Endless Wire Rope Sling row whose rating covers the load; [our wire rope sling capacity chart](/blog/wire-rope-sling-capacity-chart) lists typical wire rope sling capacities.

faqs.q: What load rating does the Endless Wire Rope Sling carry?
faqs.a: For the Endless Wire Rope Sling the table gives working loads in kN by hitch. At 114 mm it lists 1140 kN single, 2060 kN double at 45 and 4120 kN four-leg at 45, against a minimum breaking load of 6875 kN. Choose on the hitch you will rig; see [our sling angle chart](/blog/sling-angle-chart) for how the angle cuts the load.

faqs.q: What material and finish does the Endless Wire Rope Sling have?
faqs.a: The Endless Wire Rope Sling is made of steel wire rope, with eyes finished as the listing describes. For rope construction and core choices, see [our guide to wire rope construction](/blog/wire-rope-construction-explained).

faqs.q: What standard and certificate apply to the Endless Wire Rope Sling?
faqs.a: The Endless Wire Rope Sling ships with the manufacturer's test certificate for each consignment. For third-party certification or witnessed proof testing, say so on the RFQ.

faqs.q: Which parts connect to the Endless Wire Rope Sling?
faqs.a: The Endless Wire Rope Sling is used with shackles and hooks rated at least to the sling's working load limit, and with the [synthetic slings](/c/synthetic-slings) or [chain slings](/c/chain-slings) where a different sling type suits the load. [Our guide to wire rope eye terminations](/blog/wire-rope-eye-terminations) covers the eye terminations.

faqs.q: How do I install and check the Endless Wire Rope Sling?
faqs.a: Inspect the Endless Wire Rope Sling before every use for broken wires, kinks, corrosion and damaged eyes, and take it out of service if it is damaged. Slings need periodic inspection by a competent person; [our lifting equipment inspection guide](/blog/lifting-equipment-inspection-uae) sets out the routine.

faqs.q: How does the Endless Wire Rope Sling compare with the Flemish Eye Wire Rope Sling?
faqs.a: The Endless Wire Rope Sling is a different sling build from the [Flemish Eye Wire Rope Sling](/p/flemish-eye-wire-rope-sling): choose on the hitch, the load and whether the sling is endless or has formed eyes. [Our guide to types of lifting slings](/blog/types-of-lifting-slings) compares the sling types.

faqs.q: What is the Flemish Eye Wire Rope Sling and where is it used?
faqs.a: The Flemish Eye Wire Rope Sling is a Flemish eye wire rope sling to EN 13414 for lifting with cranes and hoists, listed with 1.2 to 123 t. It is rated with a 5:1 design factor between working load limit and minimum breaking load, with vertical, choker and basket ratings in each row.

faqs.q: How do I read Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling part numbers such as IH-LR-SL-TWRS-6MM?
faqs.a: IH-LR-SL-TWRS-6MM is the 6 mm size, IH-LR-SL-TWRS-28MM the 28 mm size and IH-LR-SL-TWRS-70MM the 70 mm size. The size table lists every Indus part number with its own dimensions and rating, so quote the full part number rather than the series name.

faqs.q: What size range does the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling cover?
faqs.a: The Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling is listed in sizes 6 mm to 70 mm. The size table gives each size its own Indus part number, with rope size, ratings or dimensions for that size.

faqs.q: How should I pick the size of Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling for my job?
faqs.a: Choose on the rated load for the way you will rig it: the angle between legs cuts what each leg may carry, and [our sling angle chart](/blog/sling-angle-chart) shows how. Then pick the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling row whose rating covers the load; [our wire rope sling capacity chart](/blog/wire-rope-sling-capacity-chart) lists typical wire rope sling capacities.

faqs.q: What load rating does the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling carry?
faqs.a: The listing for the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling publishes no load rating, so we do not quote one here and it must not be used to lift until the rating is confirmed in writing. Send the duty, rope size and hitch on the RFQ and we confirm the rating with the quotation; see [our wire rope sling capacity chart](/blog/wire-rope-sling-capacity-chart) for typical capacities.

faqs.q: What is the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling made from and how is it finished?
faqs.a: The Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling is made of steel wire rope (mild steel), with eyes finished as the listing describes. For rope construction and core choices, see [our guide to wire rope construction](/blog/wire-rope-construction-explained).

faqs.q: Does the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling come with a test certificate?
faqs.a: The Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling is made to EN 13414; the listing does not state a certificate, so ask on the RFQ for the documents your site needs and we confirm what can be supplied before you order.

faqs.q: Which parts connect to the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling?
faqs.a: The Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling is used with shackles and hooks rated at least to the sling's working load limit, and with the [synthetic slings](/c/synthetic-slings) or [chain slings](/c/chain-slings) where a different sling type suits the load. [Our guide to wire rope eye terminations](/blog/wire-rope-eye-terminations) covers the eye terminations.

faqs.q: How should the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling be fitted and inspected?
faqs.a: Inspect the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling before every use for broken wires, kinks, corrosion and damaged eyes, and take it out of service if it is damaged. Slings need periodic inspection by a competent person; [our lifting equipment inspection guide](/blog/lifting-equipment-inspection-uae) sets out the routine.

faqs.q: How does the Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling compare with the Four-Leg Wire Rope Sling?
faqs.a: The Two-Leg Wire Rope Sling and the [Four-Leg Wire Rope Sling](/p/four-leg-wire-rope-sling) are both EN 13414 multi-leg slings with no load rating published on the listing, and they differ in the number of legs and how the load shares between them. Confirm the rating in writing for either before use, and quote the leg count and sling angle on the RFQ.
